turns.user: Is my 3DCP mortar (w/b 0.30, s/b 1.5, 90 % OPC + 10 % silica fume, 0.6 % PCE, 0.2 % cellulose VMA) buildable for a 400 mm high, 1 m long single-filament wall printed with a 30 mm nozzle at 40 mm/s?
turns.text:
I’ll check the available buildability tools and input conventions, then assess the wall using the physical collapse, buckling, and open-time criteria.
**The screening verdict is non-printable under the assumed geometry and schedule.** Plastic collapse governs, with free-wall buckling also a concern. This is a model-based warning; measured fresh-state properties are needed to confirm it.

The calculator assumed a **15 mm layer height**, **35.53 mm filament width**, no dwell, density **2,100 kg/m³**, and load safety factor **1.5**. This gives **27 layers**, a **25 s layer cycle**, and **11.25 min** printing time.

| Physical check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plastic collapse | Expected around layer **4**, approximately **59 mm** high |
| Free-wall buckling | Expected around layer **6**, assuming elastic modulus/yield-stress ratio **25** |
| Open time | Unresolved: no measured open time supplied |

Predicted fresh properties, shown as **q50 [q10, q90]**, are:

- Static yield stress: **645 [28, 6,568] Pa**
- Structuration rate: **0.586 [0.0236, 14.518] Pa/s**

Structuration is a **weak-model, order-of-magnitude estimate**. Published analogues provide useful context: [MK10 and MK5](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2022.128808), printed with a **30 mm nozzle** and **15 mm layers**, reached **339 mm** and **311 mm** in stack-to-failure cylinder tests. Both recorded collapse; their closed geometry does not establish stability of your straight wall.

Practical changes are:

- **Increase strength development:** at the current cycle, the calculator requires initial static yield stress **6,830 Pa**, holding structuration fixed, or structuration **9.75 Pa/s**, holding initial yield stress fixed. Trial accelerator, VMA adjustment, or lower w/b, while checking extrusion.
- **Lengthen the cycle:** the plastic-collapse calculation requires at least **416 s/layer**. Its upper bound is only a database fallback; measured open time and buckling must be checked before adopting this schedule.
- **Improve geometry:** use a wider/multiple-filament wall, returns or bracing, and reassess a lower layer height.

Admixture dosages were interpreted as product mass percentages of binder. The prediction tool also defaulted to **28 d**, **comp_cube50**, and **zero rest time**; age and specimen defaults are not fresh-state validation.

Measure static yield stress, structuration, fresh stiffness and open time after representative pumping, then reassess. Final acceptance needs an experimental wall trial.
